questions.qtext: Applying DeMorgan's theorem to the expression $\overline{\overline{(\boldsymbol{X}+\boldsymbol{Y})}+\overline{\boldsymbol{Z}}}$, we get
questions.solution:
Answer: A

Selected solution (score: 1)

$\overline{ (\overline{(X+Y)}+\overline{Z}}) = \overline{ \overline{(X+Y)}} . \overline{ \overline{Z} } = (X+Y) . Z$

Hence, Option A is correct answer.

questions.qtext: The simplification of the Boolean expression $(\overline{\overline{\boldsymbol{A}} \boldsymbol{B} \overline{\boldsymbol{C}}})+(\overline{\boldsymbol{A} \overline{\boldsymbol{B}} \boldsymbol{C}})$ is
questions.solution:
Answer: B

Selected solution (score: 3)

$ \overline{(\overline{A}B\overline{C})} + \overline{(A\overline{B}C)} = ( \overline{\overline{A}} + \overline{B} + \overline{\overline{C}} )+ ( \overline{A} +\overline{\overline{B}} + \overline{C}) $

$=(\overline{\overline{A}} + {\overline{A}}) + (\overline{\overline{B}} + {\overline{B}}) + (\overline{\overline{C}} + {\overline{C}})$

$=(A + {\overline{A}}) + (B + {\overline{B}}) + (C + {\overline{C}})$

$=1+1+1$

$=1$

Hence, Option B is correct.
